purpose: Explain the remaining actual departure delay beyond deterministic clock rounding before proposing another predictor.
source: Existing server-resident v120 native commands, visits, exchanges, contexts and the existing v121/v122 labels. Read relevant existing simulator/observer code only as needed to resolve event semantics.
scope: For all11 non-clock-exact mature roots and the one60-second censored root, reconstruct command application, nominal and clock-rounded deadline, actual stop/service events, boarding/alighting and subsequent same-vehicle commands. Separate directly logged facts from inferred causes; account for the stable18 and shock16 extra seconds without assuming they are pure boarding duration.
censoring: The censored root stays censored in v121/v122 training and score. A later native event may be described only in this diagnostic timeline; it must not replace the original60-second label or enter calibration.
outputs: Compact per-root reason/timeline summaries and a judgement whether any remaining state-dependent target is observable from pre-action inputs. Keep full evidence on server; no per-root figures or broad replay.
cost_gate: Complete four days and technical checks. fresh-minus-matched-no_fresh mean<0,stable<=0,shock<0; additionally fresh-minus-same-actor-frozen<=0 in each scenario and at least one<0. Report no_fresh-minus-frozen to distinguish baseline drift. Early and tail windows are descriptive, not new gates.
decision: If mechanisms are directly computable, use that finding in a separate future service-response design; if unobservable or unresolved, retain the gap. Do not automatically fit a new residual model or deploy a controller.
